schema.description: Discriminator that identifies this JSON as a SpriteShip export manifest. Never changes.

schemaVersion.description: Semver-like schema version. Additive changes bump the minor (1.0 → 1.1); breaking changes bump the major (1.x → 2.0). Consumers should pin the major.

exportedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when this bundle was generated.

appUrl.description: Canonical app URL. Stable across exports.

source.description: Origin of this export. Lets downstream tools (and AI assistants) attribute the asset correctly.

title.description: Human-readable display name for the exported entity.

entityId.description: Stable SpriteShip ID for the entity (character/asset/map). Survives renames; safe to use as an idempotency key when re-importing.

engineVersion.description: Engine version this bundle was tested against. The bundle may still work in older/newer versions — this is a hint, not a hard requirement.

path.description: Path relative to the zip root. Matches the actual file in this archive. Use this to locate the file from your engine code or build script.

role.description: Role of this file. `engine-*` roles are engine-native and consumed directly by the target engine; `license`/`readme`/`preview`/`schema`/`manifest`/`skill` are the SpriteShip bundle layer shared across all engines.

description.description: One-line human-readable description of the file. Safe to display to end users or pass to an AI assistant as context.

items.description: One entry in the zip-file inventory.

files.description: Self-describing inventory of every file in this zip. Walk this array to discover what each file is for — never guess from filenames alone.

fieldWarnings.description: Map exports only, present when non-empty: custom data-field resolution warnings (e.g. a referenced entity was deleted so its fields were skipped). Mirrors the `warnings` array in fields-schema.json.

schema.description: Payload discriminator. Never changes for this export shape.

version.description: Payload version. Bumped on breaking shape changes.

gameType.description: Game type label this character was authored for: `platformer` | `topdown` | `topdown-overhead` | `isometric` | `point-and-click`. Influences animation conventions (which directions exist, anchor mode, etc.).

frameSize.description: Source frame size in pixels. Equals `sourceSize.w` of every atlas frame — Phaser reads it for `frame.realWidth`, `displayOriginX`, and body/scale math. Single source of truth for the renderer's pixel space.

row.description: Starting spritesheet row for this animation.

frameCount.description: Number of curated frames in this animation.

fps.description: Default playback rate in frames per second.

loop.description: Whether the animation loops by default.

holdFrame.description: Optional frame index to hold for authored timing.

loopStart.description: Frame index where the loop body starts.

loopEnd.description: Frame index where the loop body ends.

displayName.description: User-facing label; the containing object key remains the immutable animation slug.

collisionBodyMode.description: Whether collision was fitted from the first final frame or manually overridden.

movement.description: Reusable asset collider. All child coordinates are fractions of the same sprite/cell; circle radius is a fraction of width. Compound children are separate solids, not a filled bounding box. None explicitly disables collision; null/omission follows endpoint inheritance rules.

hurtbox.description: Reusable asset collider. All child coordinates are fractions of the same sprite/cell; circle radius is a fraction of width. Compound children are separate solids, not a filled bounding box. None explicitly disables collision; null/omission follows endpoint inheritance rules.

hitbox.description: Reusable asset collider. All child coordinates are fractions of the same sprite/cell; circle radius is a fraction of width. Compound children are separate solids, not a filled bounding box. None explicitly disables collision; null/omission follows endpoint inheritance rules.

cx.description: Body center X, as a fraction 0..1 of the sprite/cell width (X) or height (Y).

cy.description: Body center Y, as a fraction 0..1 of the sprite/cell width (X) or height (Y).

hw.description: Half-width (center → edge), as a fraction 0..1 of the sprite/cell width (X) or height (Y). Full width is `hw * 2`.

hh.description: Half-height (center → edge), as a fraction 0..1 of the sprite/cell width (X) or height (Y). Full height is `hh * 2`.

rot.description: Rotation in radians around the body center, clockwise-positive. Absent = 0. Use an exact-shape solver when the default engine cannot represent rotation; never replace an authored shape with its AABB.

cx.description: Circle center X, as a fraction 0..1 of the sprite/cell width (X) or height (Y).

cy.description: Circle center Y, as a fraction 0..1 of the sprite/cell width (X) or height (Y).

r.description: Radius as a fraction 0..1 of the sprite/cell WIDTH (width, not height — so the circle stays round on non-square sprites).

points.description: Closed loop of 3..64 vertices, as a fraction 0..1 of the sprite/cell width (X) or height (Y). The closing edge is implicit — do not repeat the first point. MAY BE CONCAVE.

collisionBody.description: Physics body for this animation, normalized to the full untrimmed source frame. Prefer it over the character-level body while this animation plays, and re-apply it when playback changes. Scale by frameSize/sourceSize; do not subtract spriteSourceSize or alpha-trim offsets.

startPoseId.description: Stored start-pose provenance. It does not determine collision sizing.

endPoseId.description: Stored end-pose provenance. It does not determine collision sizing.

animations.description: Flat top-level animation map across all groups. Lets consumers build a single `animConfig` without merging per-group lists. Each animation is already curated to exactly its frames — frame selection is applied at build time, so consumers never see frame-index lists.

key.description: Logical group name. Single-sheet characters always use `"default"`; per-direction characters use direction codes like `"down"`, `"up_left"`.

sheetUrl.description: Public full-resolution spritesheet URL in JSON responses, or an archive-relative canonical path containing the selected-size pixels in a narrowed zip.

atlasUrl.description: Public full-resolution atlas URL in JSON responses, or an archive-relative canonical path containing selected-size geometry in a narrowed zip. Identical content to the inline `atlas` field.

x.description: Frame X in spritesheet pixels (top-left origin).

y.description: Frame Y in spritesheet pixels (top-left origin).

frame.description: Rectangle inside the spritesheet PNG this frame occupies.

w.description: Original sprite canvas width before trimming.

h.description: Original sprite canvas height before trimming.

sourceSize.description: Original (untrimmed) sprite canvas dimensions. Use this for renderer body size, collision boxes, and scale math.

x.description: Per-frame X offset of trimmed content within the source canvas. This IS the per-frame anchor — collision math and mount-point math must read this.

y.description: Per-frame Y offset of trimmed content within the source canvas.

w.description: Width of the trimmed content rect.

h.description: Height of the trimmed content rect.

spriteSourceSize.description: Where the trimmed content sits inside the source canvas. Top-left origin. Used to recover the original sprite pivot after the exporter strips transparent padding.

duration.description: Per-frame duration in milliseconds. When set, overrides the animation-level fps for this frame (variable-pace animations).

trimmed.description: Whether transparent edges were trimmed. If true, `spriteSourceSize` carries the un-trim offset.

rotated.description: Whether the frame was rotated 90° during atlas packing. Almost always false for SpriteShip atlases.

additionalProperties.description: A single animation frame inside the atlas. Shape is identical to TexturePacker JSON Hash, so any TexturePacker-compatible runtime can load it.

frames.description: Map of frame-name → frame definition. Frame names are referenced from animations and mounts.
Frame names (keys into the atlas `frames` map) in play order.

fps.description: Default playback rate in frames per second. Can be overridden per-frame via the `duration` field on the atlas frame.

loop.description: Whether the animation loops by default. One-shot animations (`false`) hold on the last frame after one play.

loopStart.description: Frame index inside `frames[]` where the loop restarts. Allows intro + looping body in one animation.

loopEnd.description: Frame index inside `frames[]` where the loop ends. The body runs `loopStart` → `loopEnd` repeatedly.

additionalProperties.description: Animation definition with a frame sequence + playback metadata.

animations.description: Map of animation-name → animation definition. The renderer plays `frames[]` at `fps` and loops per `loop`.

image.description: Filename of the spritesheet PNG this atlas refers to (relative to atlas file location).

meta.description: Atlas-level metadata. Anything not listed here is engine-tolerated extra data.

atlas.description: Phaser-style atlas (TexturePacker JSON Hash + Phaser `animations` block).

atlasUrl.description: Downscaled atlas URL — coords scaled to match the smaller sheet.

variants.description: Pre-rendered downscaled variants. Pick the size closest to your in-game render scale to save GPU memory.

previewUrl.description: Optional single-frame thumbnail URL — useful for UI lists.

animations.description: Subset of the top-level `animations` map that lives on THIS group's sheet. Identical entries; redeclared here to make per-group loading trivial.

items.description: One renderable group — a sheet + atlas + variants. Single-sheet characters have a single-element `groups[]` array with `key="default"`.

groups.description: All renderable groups. Always non-empty. Length 1 for single-sheet characters; length N for per-direction characters (one group per direction).

name.description: Mount point name. Characters are seeded with up to ten skeleton-derived slots: "head", "left_hand", "right_hand", "chest", "back", "belt", "left_shoulder", "right_shoulder", "left_foot", "right_foot" — plus any custom slots the author added. Left/right are SCREEN sides (the slot on the visible left of the sprite), not the character's anatomy, so a slot stays on the same side of the image as the character turns. A slot is absent when the pose detector could not find it on that animation. Use this key as the slot identifier when attaching equipment sprites.

frame.description: Atlas frame name this mount is anchored to (e.g. "idle_0"). Mount coordinates are valid for THIS frame only — for animated mounts, look up the next frame's entry and interpolate, OR fetch the mount whose `frame` matches the currently-displayed frame.

x.description: X position in atlas-frame pixels, top-left origin. To get the world-space mount position: world_x = sprite_world_x + (x - sprite_pivot_x) * sprite_scale.

y.description: Y position in atlas-frame pixels, top-left origin. Apply the same transform as `x` to get world coordinates.

rotation.description: Mount rotation in radians, clockwise-positive. Apply when rendering the attached equipment sprite.

items.description: Equipment-attachment point on a character frame. Use these to spawn weapons/hats/etc. at the correct location and rotation as the character animates.

mounts.description: Equipment attachment points (weapons, hats, accessories). Same set of mounts applies across groups but coordinates are per-frame — look up each frame's entry as the character animates.

frameSize.description: Pixel space the mount coordinates are expressed in.

x.description: Mount X within the frame (top-left origin).

y.description: Mount Y within the frame (top-left origin).

slots.description: slot name → animation name → ordered per-frame mount points.

mountsData.description: Structured mount points (the canonical mounts.json shape): per-slot, per-animation, per-frame attachment coordinates. Rescale by `atlasFrameSize / frameSize` if the loaded atlas differs.

imageUrl.description: Standalone character image URL. Use this as a static fallback for image-only characters that don't yet have a built spritesheet.

prompt.description: Prompt the pose was generated from — useful as a fallback when matching direction tokens.

direction.description: Authoritative compass facing (`s` = toward camera, `e` = right profile, plus diagonals). PREFER this over token-matching `name`/`prompt` when picking a pose per facing; the text match is only the legacy fallback for poses that predate the field.

autoGenerated.description: True for pipeline-harvested poses (directional anchor set — frozen MID-STRIDE frames). When binding a facing, prefer a user pose over an autoGenerated one carrying the same direction.

collisionBody.description: Collision body authored for THIS pose specifically (normalized to the pose image). Overrides the character-level `collisionBody` while this pose is displayed. Omitted when the user authored none.

items.description: Static directional/expressive pose. Useful for image-only characters (no animations yet).

poses.description: Generated static poses. Enables image-only state machines where you swap the texture based on facing direction.

collisionBody.description: Character-level fallback collision body, normalized to the full untrimmed source frame. Prefer `animations[activeName].collisionBody` during animation playback or `poses[].collisionBody` for a displayed pose. In Phaser Arcade apply rects with `body.setSize(hw*2*frameSize, hh*2*frameSize)` and `body.setOffset((cx-hw)*frameSize, (cy-hh)*frameSize)`; do not subtract atlas `spriteSourceSize`/alpha-trim offsets. Only fall back to the frame bbox when no resolved body exists.

payload.description: Phaser character payload. Pass this directly to a Phaser scene's `load.atlas` + `anims.create` calls — the field names match Phaser's API exactly.

PhaserCharacterExport.description: Top-level SpriteShip export manifest for a Phaser character bundle.
